title: Case number 10017
raw:
The clinical findings (coarse facies, disproportionate short stature, joint contractures, cardiac valve thickening, mild cognitive impairment) together with excess urinary glycosaminoglycans and the radiographs showing classic dysostosis multiplex (thickened calvarium, J‑shaped sella, oar-shaped ribs, hip dysplasia, bullet-shaped phalanges, vertebral body beaking and cervical spine abnormalities) are characteristic of mucopolysaccharidoses in general, not specifically of Maroteaux‑Lamy or other storage diseases like GM1 gangliosidosis or CDG syndromes.

Answer: B

title: Case number 10025
raw:
The images show a solitary right frontoparietal ring-enhancing lesion with extensive surrounding edema. On diffusion-weighted imaging the center of the lesion is markedly hyperintense with corresponding low signal on the ADC map, indicating restricted diffusion of the central contents—typical for pus. This pattern (ring-enhancing lesion with central diffusion restriction) is classic for a pyogenic brain abscess rather than tumor, tuberculoma, or neurocysticercosis.

Answer: C

title: Case number 10066
raw:
The imaging studies show a large, well-circumscribed cystic adnexal mass occupying much of the pelvis, displacing adjacent structures (bladder/rectum). In a 15‑year‑old girl with sudden onset lumbar–pelvic pain and mild inflammatory markers, this is most consistent with an ovarian cyst complicated by torsion. The other options (PID, mesenteric lymphadenitis, gastroenteritis, ruptured follicle) would not produce this large adnexal cystic mass, nor the characteristic acute presentation from twisting of an adnexal mass.

Answer: A

title: Case number 10071
raw:
The patient is immunocompromised (CLL, high‑dose steroids) and presents with fever, chest pain, hemoptysis and soft‑tissue/axillary involvement.  

CT shows multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, many subpleural, some cavitary and with surrounding consolidation, without a dominant apical focus or classic tree‑in‑bud pattern. There is no typical sarcoid‐type perilymphatic nodularity or large neoplastic mass.  

In an immunosuppressed patient, this pattern of multiple cavitary nodules and disseminated soft‑tissue/lymph node involvement is most characteristic of pulmonary nocardiosis rather than aspergillosis or tuberculosis.  

Answer: B

title: Case number 10112
raw:
The imaging shows a large, predominantly cystic suprarenal mass on the left, displacing the kidney. It has internal septation/debris and lacks solid, vascular tumor components on Doppler or MRI. Grossly, it is a thick-walled hemorrhagic cyst. Histology demonstrates a fibrous wall with organizing hemorrhage and no true epithelial or endothelial lining—features characteristic of an adrenal pseudocyst and representing the chronic sequela of an antenatal adrenal hemorrhage, rather than a simple adrenal cyst or cystic neuroblastoma/lymphangioma.

Answer: A
